The site's own estimator quoted 119 credits for a 720p five-second Seedance 2.5 clip, so a Pro month at that setting is roughly 15 clips rather than 100. Check the estimate in the workspace before you generate.
What happens to my photos and clips?

The site is explicit that it stores them and vague about for how long. Generation records including portrait uploads and reference videos are "retained according to product settings and operational needs", outputs may be kept "for a limited window", and there is no self-service deletion - you email support and the policy warns there is no completion email. Whether uploads are used for model training is not stated for anything except Google sign-in data.
Who runs it and where are they?

That is not disclosed. The privacy policy names the controller only as "Company : AI Genjutsu", which is the brand; there is no registered entity, address or jurisdiction, and the Terms' governing-law clause points at "the jurisdiction where AI Genjutsu is established" without naming one. Payment runs through Stripe.
trial_checklist: Spend the 18 free credits on the one workflow you actually need, and note the estimate first: at the default Seedance 2.5 720p/5s setting a single clip was quoted at 119 credits, so the free balance will not cover it - switch to a short, low-resolution Kling motion-control job to test inside the free tier
Judge the output on the two things motion transfer usually breaks: whether the new face stays consistent through fast movement, and whether hands, reflections and background edges hold
Compare one preset against your own uploaded clip. Presets are the product's best case; your own footage is what you will actually use
Download the free render and check the watermark and resolution before deciding, since watermark-free downloads are the paid feature

Before paying anything, pick monthly rather than annual if you are testing: the annual Starter plan costs more per credit than the monthly one, and annual credits arrive as a full-year balance that expires by period

Ask support@aigenjutsu.app, in writing, who the operator is, how long portrait photos and reference videos are kept, and whether uploads are used for model training - the pages do not say, and the answer is the difference between a usable tool and an unmanageable one for client work
rating_rationale: Job fit 4.2/5 - the workspace does the thing it advertises, with a preset library that removes the hardest part of a motion-transfer job (finding the clip and knowing which photo fills which role), an honest model matrix naming Kling, Wan and Seedance and their resolution ceilings, a visible credit estimate, and a refund policy with real arithmetic behind it. It is held below 4.5 by a free tier that is one short clip, by per-clip costs that run well above the plan cards' own maths, and by output quality we cannot verify from outside without paying. Transparency 3.5/5, and this is what pulls the entry to 3.9: no controller, company or jurisdiction is named anywhere and the governing-law clause is circular; retention carries no period and self-service deletion is switched off; model training is unstated for the photos and clips that are the product's input; processors are named by function except Stripe; and the Terms are dated ten days before the domain existed. Against that, the site discloses non-affiliation with Higgsfield in five places, forbids face swaps and non-consensual impersonation, gates analytics behind a consent control, and publishes a refund calculation rather than a promise - which is why this sits at the bottom of the 3.8-4.2 band for a real but unproven entrant rather than below it.

Two ways to buy. The site gives three answers, and we are recording the contradiction rather than resolving it in the vendor's favour. The footer Terms name UME Technology Inc.; the store policy page for terms names Huasengdi Technology Co., Ltd. of Sheridan, Wyoming as the administrator and the entity accountable for data under the EULA; and both governing-law clauses say 'the laws of the United States' without naming a state. UME Technology Inc. is a real Colorado company (registration 20251272831, in good standing) and the vendor has confirmed in writing that it is the seller and operator, that 1312 17th St, Unit 2955, Denver is the current address and that Colorado law governs. Until that reaches the pages, treat the contracting party as UME Technology Inc. on the vendor's written word, not on the terms you are asked to accept.
Can it record phone calls, and is that legal where I live?

The Plus and ONE have a dedicated call mode that captures both sides of a phone conversation, which is the job meeting bots cannot do at all. Legality is on you: call-recording rules differ by state and country, several US states require every party to consent, and some countries require it of all parties regardless of where you are calling from. The product pages and the terms carry no consent warning at all - the only mention on the site is a blog post about one-party and all-party consent laws - so check your jurisdiction before recording anyone.
How does this compare with Otter, Fireflies or Fathom?

Those are meeting bots: they join your video call as a participant, produce a transcript, and are free or inexpensive to start. UMEVO is a physical recorder that captures rooms and phone calls, costs $79-$159 up front, and puts nothing in the attendee list. If your meetings are on Zoom or Teams with a laptop open, a meeting bot is cheaper and easier. If the conversations that matter happen in a room, on a phone call, or somewhere a laptop would be intrusive, a recorder is the only one of the two that can do the job.

faq: What is AccurateScribe.ai?

A transcription and subtitle service. You upload audio or video (up to 10 hours and 5GB per file), paste a public URL, or record in the browser, and it returns text in 134+ languages with speaker identification and export to DOCX, PDF, TXT, CSV, SRT or VTT. It also converts media to MP3/WAV and includes a screen recorder that transcribes what it captures. It has been live since November 2024 and ships as a web app, an iOS app, a Chrome extension, a Microsoft Store app, a ChatGPT app and a Google Workspace add-on.
How much does AccurateScribe.ai cost?

One paid plan, unlimited: $9.99/month billed annually at $119.99/year, or $19.99 month-to-month. There is no minutes allowance to track on either - 'Unlimited transcription usage' and 'Unlimited subtitle generation' are listed on both cards. A free tier returns partial transcripts and basic features without a card. The same three figures ($9.99, $119.99, $19.99) appear on the /ar/pricing locale mirror as on the English page. PayPal is named on the pricing page.
Is there a free plan?

Yes, but it is a restricted one rather than a full trial: the FAQ describes it as letting free users 'view partial transcripts and use basic features'. That is enough to judge accuracy on your own audio; it is not enough to produce a finished transcript.
Who owns my transcripts?

You keep your rights in the recordings, files and transcripts you upload or generate - the Terms say 'You retain your rights to the recordings, files and transcripts you upload'. But the licence the site takes is thin on the output side: it grants you 'a limited, non-exclusive license' to use the service and to download and store results, and does not state affirmatively that the transcript is yours to license onward. If you need output ownership in writing for client work, ask them before you rely on it.
Does AccurateScribe train AI models on my recordings?

It says no, and extends the denial to its processors: 'We do not use this content to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve our own or third parties' AI models, and we do not permit third-party service providers processing this content on our behalf to use it for those purposes.' It also states there is no human review of recordings or transcripts. What it does not state is what OpenAI - named as its AI service provider - does with the audio under OpenAI's own terms.
How long are my files kept?

The policy gives actual periods rather than a phrase: original uploads are deleted automatically after processing completes; MP3 files extracted or generated during processing are retained 30 days by default and then deleted; transcript text and the audio associated with results stay in your account for you to manage and delete, and the policy says the 30-day default does not apply to them. Deletion is described as permanent, with no backups.
Can I get a refund?

No. The return policy is explicit that 'all purchases are final and non-refundable, regardless of whether the service has been used', and that 'canceling a subscription does not generate a refund for the current billing period'. You can cancel at any time to stop future renewals. If you are in the UK or EU, a blanket no-refund term on a digital service may not be enforceable against you, but nothing on the site offers a cooling-off period - test on the free tier before paying.
Who runs AccurateScribe.ai?

The site does not say. No company name, registered address, jurisdiction or governing-law clause appears on any page, and the footer carries only a copyright line. The operator also runs WhisperTranscribe.ai and WhisperTranscript.ai - the three share a legal template, a tool route set, a mail provider, a hosting address and a registrar, and accuratescribe.com redirects to this domain - and both Whisper brands are held from listing pending verification of their names and of a single-listing-or-several decision.
Does AccurateScribe have an affiliate programme?

Yes, and it is published on the site: 40% commission on subscriptions, payouts weekly on Fridays by PayPal or bank, no follower requirement, and real-time conversion analytics. The page also states 'Our partners earn an average of $10,000+ monthly', which is an earnings claim with no basis published behind it.

faq: What is Makify AI?

A browser-based AI image editor and generator aimed at product and marketing visuals. You upload a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 30MB, describe the edit in plain English, and it returns product scenes, listing images, ads, mockups and infographics using third-party models including OpenAI's GPT Image line, Google's Nano Banana family, Seedream 5.0 and FLUX 3. The same credit balance also buys short videos from Seedance, MiniMax, Kling and Wan. It was previously sold as AI GPT Image, and the in-app notice confirms existing accounts and credits moved across.
How much does Makify AI cost?

Free to start with 30 sign-up credits and additional 7-day check-in credits. Subscriptions run $11.90/month (Basic, 100 credits/month) and $29.90 (Standard, 300), with a Pro slider from $59.90 (750) to $159.90 (2,300); billed annually those become $118.80, $238.80 and $358.80-$958.80 a year, which is 17%, 33% and 50% below the monthly equivalents. One-time packs run from $9.90 for 80 credits to $199 for 2,500 and expire after 6 months, and subscribers can buy top-ups from $29.90 for 300 credits to $899 for 12,500. A one-week Starter Pass of 40 credits costs $4.99.
How are credits used up?

Per generation, at a rate published on the pricing page for each model and setting: 3 credits for a GPT Image 2 image, 4 for GPT Image 2.5/2.6 variants, 8 for Nano Banana Pro, and 25 to 125 credits per 5-second video clip depending on model. The pricing page states the same billing engine charges the account, so the table and the deduction should match - our reading is that the ladder is consistent, but nothing here has been tested hands-on.
Can I use the images commercially?

The marketing copy says yes on paid plans: the homepage says paid plans 'include a commercial license for your store, ads and client work' and the pricing FAQ repeats it. The Terms do not carry that promise - section 6 says whether an output can be used 'depends on applicable law, your inputs, the rights of third parties, and the terms of the third-party models involved' and that 'we do not guarantee that any output is eligible for copyright protection or can be used commercially in every situation'. Treat the commercial licence as unconfirmed in writing until the vendor says which document governs, especially for client deliverables.
Who runs Makify AI, and how long are my uploads kept?

The footer of every page says the site is 'operated by ARKELUMA LLC'; no other identity appears. The privacy policy names no controller, postal address or governing law, states no retention period for uploads or outputs, and never says whether submitted images are used for training. Contact is support@makifyai.com (the submission also used contact@makifyai.com, and the domain's Cloudflare mail routing accepts both). If you are uploading client product photography, get retention in writing before you start.

best_for: Creators and small teams who already have a reference image and need a written brief for it: illustrators testing an art direction, designers producing concept variants, marketers fixing a campaign's visual language from a moodboard, and hobbyists learning how image prompts are structured. It fits the free-and-anonymous case well - no account, eight output languages, model-specific formatting for Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Flux and Nano Banana - and it fits someone who wants one editable paragraph rather than four variants at once. summary: AI Image to Prompt is a free browser tool that reads an uploaded image and writes the text prompt that would recreate something like it, formatted for the image model you name. You supply a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 8MB by drag-and-drop, file picker, clipboard paste or public image URL, pick an output style (General, Nano Banana, Flux, Midjourney with comma-separated descriptors and parameters, or Stable Diffusion with tags and a suggested negative prompt), and optionally an output language from eight options, then copy an editable result. A text-to-prompt mode handles the same job without an image, and a prompt history is kept in the browser. No account is required and the site says uploads are deleted after processing, with generation run through kie.ai on Cloudflare infrastructure. It describes visible elements - subject, setting, composition, perspective, lighting, palette, style, mood - and the site is explicit that it does not recover the original hidden prompt behind an AI image, only a reproduction-oriented approximation. Verification was read-only: the /api/generate route is live and rejects an empty body with 400 {"error":"no_image"}, but no generation was run, so output quality is not assessed here.

faq: Is AI Image to Prompt actually free?

Yes, and the claim is consistent across the homepage, the FAQ, the Terms and llms.txt: no account, no download and no credit card. The caution is that the site's /pricing route does not describe this tool at all - it still serves the ShipAny SaaS-boilerplate plans ($99/$199/$299 per month, or $89/$169/$249 billed annually) with 'Get ShipAny' buttons. Treat the tool as free and ignore that route until the vendor replaces it.
Does it recover the original prompt behind an AI-generated image?

No, and the site says so itself: it 'generates a close, similar prompt rather than the exact original', because 'the true prompt behind an AI image cannot be known for certain'. What you get is a description of visible elements - subject, setting, composition, perspective, lighting, palette, style and mood - written in the format your target model prefers.
Which image models does the output target?

Five styles are selectable: a General prompt that works across models, Nano Banana, Flux, Midjourney (comma-separated descriptors with parameters) and Stable Diffusion (tags plus a suggested negative prompt). The site also lists ChatGPT and Gemini as destinations for the general style. Prompt history is kept in browser local storage, not on a server.
What happens to my uploaded image?

The privacy policy states that uploads are temporarily stored to process the request and deleted immediately after the prompt is generated, that generated prompts stay in browser local storage rather than on the server, and that server logs are kept for up to 30 days. The image is sent to kie.ai for processing, which the notice names and then defers to for that provider's own handling - so the deletion and no-training assurances depend on kie.ai's terms as well as this site's.
Who operates the site, and what law applies?

Neither is stated. There is no company name, registration number, postal address or named controller on any page, and the governing-law clause reads only 'applicable laws, without regard to conflict of law provisions'. The only published address is a personal Gmail in the privacy policy and Terms. If you need a contracting counterparty before uploading client material, that is the item to resolve first.

Not that we can see. Six five-star quotes from named people with job titles are presented without any source, link, date or disclaimer, on a site registered 2026-07-05. We publish this as an unverified claim rather than as evidence of use.

name: AgentMsgr

summary: AgentMsgr is a messaging app for AI agents you already run elsewhere. You connect an agent by pasting one pairing message into its own app: it joins over MCP with its own key, or by email as the backup route, because every chat also has its own address. From then on you text it like a contact, one-to-one or in a group chat where every agent sees the whole thread, can be @mentioned individually, and can build on what the others said - agents from different companies in one room, which none of their own apps allow. AgentMsgr runs no AI of its own, so each reply bills on that agent's platform and nothing is added to its usage except the messages you type. A second MCP endpoint lets your own Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or Perplexity post briefs and read replies as you, with an Allow / read-only choice. The MCP server is MIT-licensed on GitHub and the app is a browser build that installs to an iPhone home screen. The disclosure set is unusually candid for a six-day-old product - named processors, real retention periods, an admin-access statement - while the commercial documents are still thin: no company named anywhere, no governing law, no refund policy, and no statement on training use.

faq: What is AgentMsgr?

A messaging app for AI agents you already use on other platforms. You paste one pairing message into an agent's own app, it connects over MCP with its own key or joins by email, and you then text it one-to-one or in a group chat where agents from different companies see the same thread and can build on each other's answers. AgentMsgr runs no AI: each agent answers from its own account, tools, memory and subscription.
How much does AgentMsgr cost?

Free covers up to 3 agents, 1 group chat, 100 messages a day, 250 MB of files and full message history. Pro is $10.49 a month at launch against a $29.99 list price, with unlimited agents and group chats, 150 messages an hour and 3,000 a week, and 5 GB of files, cancelled from Manage billing. Only messages you type count against the limits; agents' replies do not. A Teams tier is listed as 'Later' and is not sold yet.
How is this different from a multi-AI chat app?

A multi-AI app rents you several models side by side and charges for the tokens. AgentMsgr connects the agents you already pay for on their own platforms and charges only for the messaging layer, so quality, tools and memory are whatever your agents already have, and nothing is added to their usage except the messages you send them.
Does connecting an agent use up its usage limits?

Each reply your agent sends counts on its own platform, exactly as if you had messaged it there. What AgentMsgr adds is the message you type. The vendor notes that a watcher that polls for new messages uses more of the agent's usage than a wake link or an inbox that wakes it on new mail, which is why the pairing message asks the agent to set up instant notification first.

faq: What is 01Router?

An API gateway that puts one key in front of several AI model vendors. You send a model id, optionally a provider, and your input to /api/v1/generations; 01Router forwards the job to one of ten upstream routes and bills the credits at 100 to the dollar. The same key covers video, image, audio and chat models, and a projects feature lets you resell those models to your own users at a markup you set.
How much does 01Router cost?

No subscription. Credits cost $1 per 100, sold in one-time packs of 1,000 credits for $10 up to 525,000 credits for $5,000 (a 5% bonus), valid 365 days. What a job costs depends on the model and provider: Seedance 2.5 at 480p runs from $0.055 to $0.126 a second depending on which provider serves it, and the same model at 1080p from $0.508 to $0.702 a second. It resells ByteDance, Alibaba, Google, Kuaishou and xAI models with no non-affiliation line anywhere, and OpenRouter - the larger router its name sits one word away from - appears as one of the ten upstream providers in its own price tables. Treat the model names as the model makers' trademarks and ask 01Router directly if the relationship matters to your contract.

Yes. Terms section 5 grants full commercial and non-commercial usage rights to media generated on your account, subject to the acceptable-use rules, and the FAQ repeats it. faq: Is Random Topic Generator free?

Do I need to create an account to practise speaking?

What does the AI speech report actually score?

Six weighted dimensions: grammar 20% (tense, agreement, articles, word choice), coherence 20% (thesis, structure, transitions), vocabulary 15% (diversity and register), fluency 20% (pacing and mid-sentence hesitation), filler words 10% (every um, uh, like and you know, with roughly five points off per filler per minute) and confidence. The policy commits that the operator does not use your recordings for anything other than delivering the analysis, and that recordings sit in private storage tied to your account. faq: What is Edit Pic Text?

A browser AI image text editor that changes the words already inside a photo, screenshot or design instead of adding a new text layer. You upload a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 30MB, the editor outlines the text it detects, you type the replacement (or leave it blank to delete the words), and it redraws them in the original font, size and colour with the background repaired. Paid plans add a commercial licence and watermark-free output; exports go to 1K, 2K or 4K.
How much does Edit Pic Text cost?

Monthly plans are Basic $11.90 for 100 credits, Standard $29.90 for 300 and Pro $79.90 for 1,050, with yearly billing at $118.80, $238.80 and $358.80 a year (shown as $9.90, $19.90 and $29.90 a month). One-time credit packs run from $9.90 for 80 credits to $199 for 2,500 and stay valid 183 days, and a $4.99 Starter Pass gives 40 credits for 7 days. An edit, translation or enhance costs 5 credits at 1K and text extraction costs 1, so a $11.90 month is about 20 edits.
Is there a free tier?

Yes, and it is small but recurring. Signing in with Google grants 3 credits, and a daily check-in ladder adds 3, 3, 6, 3, 3, 3 and 9 over the first week for 30 in total - which is the number behind the 'Get 30 credits for free' badge. No card is required to start. Extraction at 1 credit is the cheapest way to test whether the OCR holds up on your own files.
Can I edit text in a screenshot, poster or product photo?

That is the core use case. The screenshot page keeps the interface, icons and spacing intact while you swap a label or heading; the poster and product-label path is for prices, dates and offers on images whose design file you no longer have. What the site refuses is documents: IDs, passports, certificates, receipts and payment screenshots are excluded in its own documentation, and edits meant to mislead are not allowed.
Does it work in languages other than English?

The site says English and other Latin-alphabet languages work best and that Chinese, Japanese and Hindi are supported, and it sells a dedicated translation page that returns the image in the original font and layout across 110 languages. Because the tool redraws type rather than overlaying it, quality depends on the script and the original lettering - very small text, curved text and heavily stylised lettering are the cases it warns may need several attempts.
What should I check before paying?

Two things on the site itself. Ask which refund threshold applies, because the pricing FAQ says a refund survives up to 50 used credits while the refund policy says 10. And read the plan you are buying carefully: the comparison table on the pricing page prices video models this product does not sell and puts an edit at 3 credits where the editor charges 5, so the editor's own meter is the number to trust.

name: Savingy

price: Free core with no card and no time limit: unlimited manual income and expense records, one-line entry, receipts, statement import, the tracker and money screens, monthly budgets and plans, goals and contributions, bill reminders, the Weekly Reset review, Ask Savingy, recurring purchases, calculators, and data backup/restore/export. Pro is sold as fixed access periods in INR, one payment each: Rs 149 for 30 days, or Rs 1,188 for 365 days - printed as about Rs 99 a month paid once, saving Rs 600 against twelve 30-day periods (12 x 149 = 1,788). A one-time 45-day Pro trial opens after 30 real expense or income entries, at the user's choosing, with no card and no charge when it ends. All prices include GST per the store listing. No purchase was attempted.
rating_rationale: Job fit 4.1, transparency 3.6, overall 3.9. Job fit is high because the free core is genuinely unlimited, the two Pro prices are checkable on three independent surfaces (the pricing page, the Google Play listing and the hardcoded amounts in the shipped checkout bundle), the arithmetic reconciles (12 x Rs 149 = Rs 1,788 against Rs 1,188 for a year, i.e. Rs 99 a month and Rs 600 saved), no bank link is asked for, and the company is identified with a CIN, a director, a street address and a West Bengal governing-law clause. Transparency is marked down for a legal set that names a different counterparty ('Savingy, Inc.') than the operating company, a refund page that still describes a renewing subscription and a cancel-before-renewal warning the product does not sell, Terms that advertise Basic/Pro/Expert plans that do not exist, no stated training use for financial text sent to OpenAI, and a family SKU priced inside the checkout bundle for a feature the site says is not available yet. Every deduction is a dated page a reader can check, and none of them changes what the product does.
summary: Savingy is an India-first expense tracker that turns what you log into one number - what is safe to spend today - plus a runway to month end, a monthly plan with budgets and goals, and a Sunday check-in it calls the Weekly Reset. Entry is manual by design: one line such as 'chai 40 upi', a receipt photo, a PDF, CSV or Excel statement import you review before anything is saved, or voice on Pro. There is no bank linking and it never asks for a banking password or PIN. The free core is not a trial - unlimited records, budgets, goals, the Weekly Reset, tracker history, reports and export cost nothing - and Pro is sold as fixed access, not a subscription: Rs 149 for 30 days or Rs 1,188 for 365 days, one payment each, with nothing renewing automatically. A one-time 45-day Pro trial opens after 30 real expense or income entries, at the user's choosing, with no card. The web app is the same product as the Android app on Google Play (com.rhnmaheshwari.savingy, updated 11 October 2026), which prints the same two prices and the same 'no subscription and no automatic renewal' line. The operator is Savingy Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (CIN U62013WB2025PTC282100), Tower House, 2A Chowringhee Square, Kolkata 700069, with Rohan Maheshwari named as director, and a Security & Trust Center that names its subprocessors - Microsoft Azure and MongoDB Atlas in Central India, Razorpay for payments, OpenAI for the assistant. The gap a buyer should know about is documentation drift rather than the product: the Privacy Policy and Terms still call the counterparty 'Savingy, Inc.', the December 2024 refund policy describes a renewing subscription the site does not sell, and the Terms still advertise Basic, Pro and Expert plans that do not exist.

Ltd., CIN U62013WB2025PTC282100, director Rohan Maheshwari, a Kolkata street address, a phone number and [personal address withheld]; the Terms fix governing law to West Bengal with Kolkata courts; and the Google Play developer block independently names the same person and a Kolkata address

The Security & Trust Center names every subprocessor with a purpose and a location - Microsoft Azure (cloud hosting, Central India), MongoDB Atlas (managed database, Central India), Razorpay (payment processing, India) and OpenAI (LLM-assisted analytics, provider-managed regions) - plus HSTS, JWT in sessionStorage, and a named security desk for DPDP grievances. Most listings here name no processor at all

cons: The legal pages name a different company than the site does. The Privacy Policy and Terms both define the counterparty as 'Savingy, Inc.' ("'Savingy,' 'we,' 'us' or 'our'") and print 'Address: Savingy, Inc., 2A Chowringhee Square, Kolkata, WB, 700069, India', while every footer on the site reads 'SAVINGY SOLUTIONS PVT. LTD. Manual-first logging: one-line entry ('chai 40 upi', 'uber 230 yesterday'), receipt photos, multiple accounts and pots, and bulk statement import from PDF, CSV or Excel with a review step before saving

faq: What does Savingy cost?

The free tier is free for good with no card: unlimited income and expense records, budgets, goals, the Weekly Reset, history, reports and export. Pro is sold as fixed access, not a subscription - Rs 149 for 30 days or Rs 1,188 for 365 days, one payment each, nothing renewing automatically - and the same two prices appear on the Google Play listing. When a paid period ends you drop back to Free and keep all your data. A one-time 45-day Pro trial opens after 30 real expense or income entries, at your choosing, with no card.
Is the trial automatic, and does it need a card?

No card and no automatic charge, per the pricing FAQ. The trial unlocks after 30 real entries and you start it when you choose; the copy says it opens with the first thing Pro notices in those entries or three weeks later at the latest. If you do nothing when it ends, Pro stops and the account returns to Free with the data intact. Buying afterwards is a single Razorpay payment for a fixed 30- or 365-day period.
Do I have to link my bank account?

No. The site states on the homepage, the security page and in the FAQ that it does not link to internet banking and does not ask for banking passwords or PINs. Tracking runs on what you enter, on receipt photos, and on statement files you upload and review yourself. That also means the numbers are only as complete as your logging - the product's own copy is careful to call the output estimates, and logging alone does not guarantee savings.
Which company am I actually buying from?

The footer names Savingy Solutions Pvt. Ltd., CIN U62013WB2025PTC282100, Tower House, 1st Floor, 2A Chowringhee Square, Kolkata 700069, with Rohan Maheshwari as director and founder, and the Terms set governing law to West Bengal with Kolkata courts. The Privacy Policy and Terms, however, name 'Savingy, Inc.' as the counterparty. We asked the vendor which entity is authoritative; until that is corrected, treat the Indian company in the footer and on the Google Play developer block as the operator.
What happens to my data if I stop paying, and can I get it out?

Nothing is deleted when Pro ends - the help page says you keep entries, budgets, goals, bill reminders and your history of closed months, and only the Pro screens lock. Data management offers backup, restore and export on every account, and the delete-data page documents an in-app deletion request with a 7-day confirmation window, after which the account, records, receipts and profile are erased, with payment records kept without name or email for the period tax law requires.

Open one statement import and check what it does with a month you already know: the import must be reviewable line by line before saving, and a wrong category or a double-counted transfer is the first thing to catch

If you pay, pay for 30 days first. The 30-day pass tests the whole Pro surface for Rs 149 and avoids committing Rs 1,188 to a product whose legal pages are all dated before the current pricing

name: Reply Argus
best_for: iOS and Android developers, app studios and agencies who would rather answer App Store and Google Play reviews in the reviewer's own language than paste the same English template at every 1-star - especially teams that want an approval gate before anything posts to a store, and developers who want the review queue reachable from an AI agent over MCP or from their own read-only REST integration
price: No self-serve free plan is published on /pricing, which sells three monthly-or-yearly plans and Enterprise: Indie $9.99/mo or $99.90/yr ($8.33/mo billed annually) with 4 active apps and 300 replies/mo; Pro $19.99/mo or $199.90/yr ($16.66/mo) with 10 active apps and 2,000 replies, adding automation rules, auto-translate, analytics, the public REST API and signed webhooks; Studio $99/mo or $990/yr ($82.50/mo) with 30 active apps and 8,000 replies, white-label sending domain and per-app isolation; Enterprise custom. Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial and the card is required at signup: the pricing FAQ answers 'You add a card to begin, but nothing is charged until day 14'. Seats are included rather than sold (5 / 10 / 25 / unlimited) and viewers are free; the FAQ states 'You're never billed for overage'. Yearly billing is exactly ten months of the monthly price (2 months free), so 9.99x10 = 99.90, 19.99x10 = 199.90 and 99x10 = 990 all reconcile. The same three prices appear in /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and the pricing page's JSON-LD Offer array. Two add-ons are described in the Terms (extra active-app slots billed on the regular cycle, and prepaid reply top-up packs that do not expire) but neither carries a price on /pricing. The vendor contradicts this on its own signup and login pages, which read 'Free for 1 app and 100 replies a month. You don't need a card', and the pricing FAQ answers 'Is there a free plan? No'. No purchase or trial was started; billing is by Dodo Payments as merchant of record.
rating_rationale: Job fit 4.3, transparency 3.6, overall 4.0. Job fit is high: the product is live and coherent, the three published prices are the same numbers on the pricing page, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and the JSON-LD Offer array, yearly billing reconciles to ten monthly payments, seats are included instead of sold per head, the approval gate is on by default, and the technical surface is real rather than described - a read-only REST API, HMAC-signed webhooks, an OAuth-gated MCP endpoint and a security.txt are all reachable. Transparency is marked down for a legal set that names no company, no registered address, no jurisdiction and no governing law; a signup and login page that promise a card-free free plan the pricing page says does not exist; no refund or cancellation policy page on the domain; AI providers left unnamed; a retention window described as 'a short window'; and traction numbers on the homepage that a reader cannot check. Each deduction is a page anyone can open, and none of them changes what the product does.
summary: Reply Argus connects to App Store Connect and Google Play, pulls every review from both stores into one inbox, and drafts a reply in the reviewer's own language - 100+ languages, drawn from the app's own store listings, marketing page, past approved replies and any notes you add, with the cited lines shown so a draft can't invent a refund or a ship date. Nothing posts until you approve it; auto-publish is opt-in and can be scoped by rating, keyword, language or store, and on Pro and up a rules engine handles that. Alongside the inbox it clusters duplicated complaints with a match score and ranks recurring asks into a 'Signal' feed that can be exported to Notion or Sheets as a roadmap. Pricing is per reply volume rather than per seat: Indie $9.99/mo (4 apps, 300 replies), Pro $19.99/mo (10 apps, 2,000 replies, API and webhooks), Studio $99/mo (30 apps, 8,000 replies, white-label), each with a 14-day trial and a card at signup. For teams that want the queue inside an agent, /api/mcp is a remote MCP server signed in over OAuth, and /api/v1 exposes read-only apps and reviews with signed webhooks. The gaps a buyer should know about are documentary: no company, address or governing law anywhere on the site, no refund policy page, unnamed AI providers, and a signup page that advertises a free plan the pricing page denies.
use_cases: Answering every App Store and Google Play review in the language it was written in, without a translator or a template library
Keeping a 1-star from sitting unanswered overnight - a shared inbox for both stores with drafts waiting on approval
Turning repeated complaints into a ranked fix list (Signal) and exporting it to Notion or Sheets as a product roadmap
Running reviews for a portfolio of apps or client apps, each with its own voice, rules and knowledge base
Letting a Claude, Cursor or Codex agent triage and draft replies over MCP with publishing still gated on approval
Pulling reviews and replies into your own tooling through the read-only REST API and signed webhooks
pros: The prices are the same three numbers on four independent surfaces - /pricing, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and the page's own JSON-LD Offer array - and the yearly figure is exactly ten monthly payments, so the '2 months free' line is arithmetic rather than a claim

Seats are bundled on every plan (5 / 10 / 25 / unlimited) and viewers are free, with the FAQ stating 'You're never billed for overage': usage is bounded by pausing drafting when the reply allowance runs out, not by an automatic upcharge

The approval gate is the default, not an option: auto-publish is off until you enable it and can be limited to 5-star replies or scoped by rating, keyword, language or store on Pro and up - which matters because both stores allow exactly one public reply per review

Grounding is shown rather than asserted: a draft displays the store-listing lines and notes it drew on, and the product flags contradictions between the app's own sources before they reach a public reply

Privacy names its processors with the job each does - Supabase (database and auth), Vercel (hosting), Jina AI (page text extraction), Resend (transactional email), Dodo Payments (billing), PostHog and Google Ads for optional analytics - and states that review text is not used to train shared models

Card data never reaches their servers (Dodo Payments is the merchant of record), and the security page invites independent scanning (Qualys SSL Labs, MDN HTTP Observatory, SecurityHeaders) instead of asking to be taken on trust
A free, no-account reply generator and calculators sit in front of the paid product, so a reader can see the drafting quality without a card
cons: No company is named anywhere on the site. The Privacy Policy and Terms both define the counterparty only as '"Reply Argus," "we," "us" or "our"', the only address published is support@replyargus.com, and there is no registered office, company number or named controller - so a buyer cannot tell which legal person they are contracting with

No governing-law or jurisdiction clause exists in the Terms, whose six short sections cover accounts, acceptable use, approvals, billing, availability and changes but omit liability, indemnity, termination, refunds, age limits and dispute resolution

The signup and login pages advertise a free plan the pricing page denies: both read 'Free for 1 app and 100 replies a month. You don't need a card' and 'Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial', while the pricing FAQ answers 'Is there a free plan? No, but every plan starts with a 14-day free trial. You add a card to begin' - a reader cannot tell whether they are signing up to a card-free tier or a card-required trial

The Terms say trials convert to paid, that plans bill in advance and that downgrades take effect at cycle end, but nothing states a refund position - and the refund/cancellation terms sit with Dodo Payments as merchant of record

The Terms are dated 1 July 2026, one day before the domain's own registration date of 2 July 2026, and the Privacy Policy 25 August 2026 - worth asking whether the earliest date is authoritative or carried over from a template

Homepage traction figures are unverifiable from outside: '1,010+ replies drafted across 350+ apps', a 'This week' panel reading 'Drafted 82 / Published 61 / avg reply 2m18s' and a '94%' response rate, with five app avatars (Parasocial, Retrograde, Woogie, Egg Notes, Truth or Dare) that are not linked to store listings

Two paid add-ons are described in the Terms - extra active-app slots billed on your regular cycle and prepaid reply top-up packs - but neither appears with a price on /pricing, so the cost of growing past a plan is not knowable before signup
The footer 'Contact' link is a mailto to support@replyargus.com only: /contact returns 404, so there is no contact page, postal address or company-detail page to fall back on

Alerts to Slack, Telegram, Discord, email or a webhook, including rating-drop and review-spike triggers
White-label on Studio: your logo, product name and sending domain, with roll-up analytics across a client portfolio
faq: What does Reply Argus cost?

Indie is $9.99 a month or $99.90 a year for 4 active apps and 300 replies a month; Pro is $19.99 or $199.90 for 10 apps and 2,000 replies plus automation rules, the REST API and webhooks; Studio is $99 or $990 for 30 apps and 8,000 replies with white-label and per-app isolation; Enterprise is custom. Every plan carries a 14-day trial with a card at signup, billed from day 14, and the yearly price is exactly ten monthly payments. No', and the extra-app-slot and reply-top-up add-ons described in the Terms carry no published price.
Does it post replies without approval?

No, not unless you turn that on. Approval mode is the default and auto-publish is opt-in, limited to 5-star replies if you want the narrowest rule, or scoped by rating, keyword, language or store on Pro and up. That default matters because both stores allow exactly one public reply per review and Google Play exposes no delete method - the vendor's own reference pages document both constraints.
Which stores does it cover, and what does it need from them?

Apple's App Store and Google Play only - no Microsoft Store, Steam or web stores. You connect App Store Connect and the Play Console once and it polls both, because neither store pushes a webhook for a new review. The vendor's API references put the practical limits at roughly 350 characters per Play reply and the 7-day reply window on both platforms.
Who is behind it, and where is the company?

Nothing on the site says. There is no company name, no registered address, no company number and no governing-law clause in the Terms, and the only contact route published is support@replyargus.com (the footer 'Contact' link is a mailto and /contact returns 404). The domain was registered on 2 July 2026, the product launched on Product Hunt on 28 July 2026, and the blog is bylined 'The Argus Team'. Ask before paying annually.
Can an AI agent drive it?

Yes - that is a first-class feature rather than an add-on. /api/mcp is a remote MCP server that signs in over OAuth (not an API key) and is scoped to your workspace, with publish calls gated on approval; the site publishes one-click setup for Cursor and Claude Desktop and CLI/TOML snippets for Claude Code and Codex. trial_checklist: Before paying: ask support which free tier exists. The signup page promises 'Free for 1 app and 100 replies a month. You don't need a card' while the pricing FAQ says there is no free plan and the card is taken at signup - the answer decides whether you are trialling or subscribing

Connect one app you actually ship and read the first ten drafts against the reviews they answer: the grounded draft shows the listing and note lines it used, so check that those lines are real and that no refund, fix date or feature it states is invented

Set approval mode and leave auto-publish off for the first two weeks; then, if you enable it, scope it to 5-star replies only. Both stores allow one public reply per review and Play's reply cannot be deleted
Test the reply language on your worst market rather than English: paste a review in the language you actually receive and check tone and formality, not just vocabulary
Check the review-sync window on both stores at the start of the trial - neither store backfills everything, and the 7-day reply window means an old review may already be unanswerable
Use Signal on a real month and export it once to Notion or Sheets; if the ranked list does not match the complaints you already know about, the clustering is not earning its place in your workflow

Before day 14, decide on the yearly price against monthly: $99.90 vs $119.88 on Indie is a real saving but a twelve-month commitment to a company that names no legal entity and publishes no refund policy

name: Change Text in Image
best_for: Creators, e-commerce sellers and small marketing teams who need to change words already baked into a finished image - a typo on an exported ad, a price on a product shot, a date on an invitation, a label in a screenshot - without the source file, priced per edit at 10 credits with a one-time pack instead of a subscription. Also worth a look if you want a text-blur tool that provably runs on your own device. Not a fit if you need a named company and jurisdiction before paying, if you need account password recovery, if you need a committed deletion deadline for uploaded images, or if you are editing IDs, receipts, bank statements or other evidence (banned in its own acceptable-use policy).
price: One-time credit packs, USD, no subscription: Starter $14.90 for 400 credits (40 text edits, $0.37 per edit), Pro $26.90 for 1,000 credits (100 edits, $0.27), Studio $39.90 for 1,800 credits (180 edits, $0.22). Each generation costs 10 credits and new accounts get 10 free credits, which is one free edit. Credits do not expire while the account remains available, failed generations return the credits spent, and checkout runs through Waffo Pancake as merchant of record. The same figures and the same per-edit arithmetic render on the /zh mirror. Verified 2026-11-18 on /#pricing, /zh and /api/config/public.
summary: Change Text in Image does one narrow job and does it in a browser: you upload a JPG, PNG or static WebP up to 10MB / 20MP, drag a box over the words you want to replace, type the original text and the replacement, and the model redraws the wording in the font, colour and style it detected while rebuilding the background behind the old letters. Leaving the replacement empty removes the text instead. There are no font, size or colour controls, by design - the promise is an edit that looks like it was always there - and the neighbouring pages cover the same workflow for screenshots and translations, plus a blur tool that runs entirely on your device. Pricing is one-time credit packs only: $14.90 for 40 edits, $26.90 for 100 and $39.90 for 180, with 10 free credits at sign-up. The paperwork is unusually straight for this class - the operators are named as an individual with a working contact, Cloudflare, fal.ai's Nano Banana and Waffo are named by company and function, prompt screening before generation is disclosed, and the policy refuses to claim zero retention or supplier-wide no-training. What holds it back is that it says tracking is not active while Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and a third-party visitor counter all load on the policy page itself, and that no company, address or jurisdiction appears anywhere.
use_cases: Fixing a typo or a wrong name on an exported poster, flyer or invitation when the design file is gone
Updating a price, discount or date on a product photo or campaign image without reopening the layout
Changing a label, version number or heading inside an app or webpage screenshot while the UI stays intact
Swapping a headline into another language on existing artwork and keeping the original font and composition
Erasing words from an image entirely by leaving the replacement field empty
Hiding an address, phone number or price on a screenshot with the free on-device blur tool before sharing it
pros: The unit of sale is clear and the arithmetic reconciles: 10 credits per generation, 400 credits = 40 edits at $0.37 each, 1,000 = 100 at $0.27, 1,800 = 180 at $0.22, and every card prints its own per-edit price

One-time packs only - 'no subscription, automatic renewal or automatic top-up' in the Terms and 'one-time purchase, no recurring charges' under the pricing cards - so there is no renewal to cancel, and purchased credits do not expire while the account stays open

The legal set is real, dated after the domain existed (Privacy, Terms and Acceptable Use all 'Last updated' 2026-09-20/22 against a 2026-08-13 registration) and written for this product rather than pasted: uploads, edit history, credit transactions, refunds and account closure are each addressed

Processors are named by company and by job - Cloudflare for hosting and its D1 database, fal.ai's Nano Banana for the edit itself, Waffo Pancake as merchant of record - and the pre-generation step is disclosed in its own paragraph: prompts (not images) go to Waffo for a content-safety verdict, a blocked check costs no credits

It does not overclaim on the two things this class usually lies about: 'No claim of zero retention or supplier-wide exclusion from model training is made by this policy', and deletion is described as a request with an explanation of what must be kept rather than a promised deadline

Acceptable use names the abuses specifically - altered IDs, passports, visas or official seals, falsified bank statements, receipts and payment confirmations, edited chat screenshots, evidence in visa or immigration applications - and says plainly that it does not promise automatic detection of every prohibited image

The blur page's 'On your device - no image upload' label held when we checked it: loading an image and pressing Blur on /blur-text-in-image sent no request to the site's API or any third-party host (the only outbound call was Google's One Tap status check)

Output rights stay with the user: 'We do not claim ownership of your inputs or outputs merely because you use the service', with a commercial-licence question left to applicable law rather than invented
cons: Three trackers load on every page, including the privacy policy that says they do not: Google Analytics G-JYK4BVL1XP, Microsoft Clarity project zbh400t6x4 and pvuv.ai's script are in the served HTML of /privacy-policy and /terms-of-service, and a live session fired /api/analytics/events, in.pvuv.ai and t.clarity.ms/collect. The policy says 'This policy does not imply that an analytics or advertising tool is active merely because the software supports it' and that non-essential tracking will get notice and choice first - there is no consent banner and no analytics section

No company, trading name, postal address or jurisdiction appears anywhere. Privacy and Terms describe the operator only as 'an independently operated service run by an individual', with a Gmail address as the only contact, and the Terms carry no governing-law clause at all

Retention for uploaded images is explicitly uncommitted: 'We do not promise permanent cloud storage or a fixed automatic image-deletion deadline', and deletion is a manual email request whose scope the operator decides - for a product whose whole function is uploading pictures

No account recovery: /api/config/public returns password_reset_enabled:false and email_verification_enabled:false, so a buyer who mistypes an email or forgets a password has no reset path while their credits sit in that account. Turnstile is also disabled (empty site key), so sign-up has no bot check

Refunds exist only as a clause inside the Terms (/refund-policy, /refunds and /refund all 404): a full refund within 7 days only if none of that purchase's credits have been used, with partial use generally non-refundable

faq: What is Change Text in Image?

A browser editor for the words inside a finished picture rather than a text layer on top of it. You upload a JPG, PNG or static WebP up to 10MB / 20MP, draw a box around the text, enter the original wording and the replacement, and the model redraws it in the font, size, colour and style it detected while repairing the background behind the old letters. Leave the replacement empty to remove the text instead. There are no font, size or colour controls - the product's claim is that the edit should look like it was always there - and every generation costs 10 credits.
How much does Change Text in Image cost?

One-time credit packs, no subscription: Starter $14.90 for 400 credits (40 edits, $0.37 each), Pro $26.90 for 1,000 credits (100 edits, $0.27 each) and Studio $39.90 for 1,800 credits (180 edits, $0.22 each). Each generation is 10 credits, failed generations return their credits, and purchased credits do not expire while the account remains available. Checkout is hosted by Waffo Pancake. Refunds are a 7-day clause inside the Terms of Service: full refund only if none of that purchase's credits have been used.
Is there a free tier, and do I need an account?

New accounts get 10 free credits, which is exactly one generation - enough to test one real file, not enough to judge a font library. You can upload an image and select text without signing in, but generating requires an account (Google or email). The separate blur tool is free, needs no account and runs on your device: our check found no image upload when using it.
What does it not do?

It will not change the font, size or colour - only the wording - and it does not guarantee copyright, uniqueness or freedom from infringement in the output. It refuses in its own acceptable-use policy: altered IDs, passports, visas, supporting letters or official seals, falsified bank statements, receipts or payment confirmations, edited chat screenshots, and edited images submitted as authentic evidence. It is also an individual-run service with no company, postal address or governing law published, and no password-reset path.

faq: What does RapAI cost?

Three one-time credit packs: Lite $6.90 for 390 credits, Pro $14.90 for 1,000 and Ultra $29.90 for 2,200, with credits valid 365 days. A 15-second clip costs 390 credits at 480p, 825 at 720p and 2,055 at 1080p, and a 5-second 480p clip costs 130 - so the smallest pack buys exactly one 15-second 480p video, or three 5-second ones. Nothing renews automatically and there is no subscription.
Is there a free trial?

No. The FAQ says so directly - 'RapAI doesn't have a free plan right now' - and the cheapest entry is the $6.90 Lite pack. Credit cost is shown before you generate and failed runs return their credits, but there is no free render to judge quality with.
Can I see an example video before paying?

Not on the site. Every page we fetched serves still images only - there are no video elements and no .mp4 or .webm files referenced anywhere - so the output has to be judged from your own first paid render. Treat the $6.90 pack as the sample.
Can I use the videos commercially?

No, not currently. The Terms, the AI Technology Disclosure and the FAQ all state that commercial output licensing is not offered. You keep whatever rights you already hold in your photos and lyrics, and the site says to check the Terms before any commercial use - which for client work or advertising means waiting for a licence that does not exist yet.
Which AI model makes the video?

The site will not claim one. It generates through SeeAPI's 'rap-video' template and its own AI Technology Disclosure says the underlying model vendor and version 'have not been disclosed in the template documentation available to us' and that it cannot substantiate Veo, Kling, Seedance or any other named model. That is an honest answer rather than a borrowed brand name, but it also means quality cannot be predicted from the model.
How long are my photos kept?

Uploaded photos are stored in Cloudflare R2 and deleted automatically 7 days after upload, with Cloudflare usually completing removal about a day later; re-uploading the same image in that window reuses the copy without extending the clock. You can email for earlier deletion. Finished videos are held through SeeAPI's links, whose retention is set by SeeAPI rather than by RapAI.
What do I need to supply?

One clear, front-facing photo of both performers (or two portraits, one per person), plus optionally a background. JPG, PNG or WEBP, up to 10 MB each, and you need permission from everyone in the photo - the terms make that your responsibility.
Who operates RapAI?
Tom Lai, named as the operator in both the Terms and the Privacy Policy. No company, postal address or governing-law clause is published, and the only contact route is support@airapvideo.design.

rating_rationale: Job fit 4.2/5. The product does one job and describes it precisely: two performers from one photo or two portraits, 4 to 15 seconds, three rap modes including your own lyrics, ratio chosen before generation, and a credit cost quoted on the button before you commit. The pricing ladder is internally consistent in a way most of this catalogue is not - 390 credits for 15 seconds at 480p, 825 at 720p, 2,055 at 1080p, and the studio's own 5-second default at 130 credits, exactly one third - so a buyer can compute the real cost of the render they want (about $5.30-$6.90 for a 15-second 480p clip). The workflow needs no account beyond Google sign-in and no editing skills. It loses points because no example output is published anywhere: on a video product that is the single most useful thing a buyer could be shown, and its absence means the first paid render is the trial. Transparency 3.6/5. Strong for what it volunteers and weak for what it does not. In its favour: the operator is named, photo retention is a stated seven-day period with a described deletion path, SeeAPI, Cloudflare R2 and Microsoft Clarity are named by company and job, there is a real refund policy with a seven-day deadline and an explicit statement that used packs are not refundable, an AUP that admits review is report-based rather than claiming pre-screening, and an AI disclosure that refuses to name a model it cannot verify - which is the honest direction to fail. Password reset and email verification are both switched off while credits sit in the account. Overall 3.9/5: a specific, honestly-priced product with better-than-average documentation and a disclosure gap on exactly the pages meant to close it.
