Can I hear the song before I pay?

Partly - you can hear 30 seconds of each of the two versions for free, and the lyric draft is free and editable. Full playback and the MP3 downloads unlock with a paid pack. That is enough to judge whether the song feels personal, but not enough to judge the whole arrangement, so treat the preview as a fit check rather than a full audition.
Is there a free trial or a free plan?

No trial of the paid product. The free path is the lyric draft plus the 30-second previews, and it is 'subject to rolling 24-hour limits and daily capacity' with no published allowance. If you need to compare several songs in one session, expect the preview budget to be the constraint.
Who runs MeloLetter, and where is it based?

Not stated. Neither the Privacy Policy (last updated September 23, 2026) nor the Terms (September 21, 2026) names a company, an individual, a country or a governing law, and there is no postal address. Support runs through support@meloletter.com, which is also the contact for data requests and content-safety reports.
Can I get a refund?

There is no refund policy page - /refund 404s - and the Terms say only that payments 'are not automatically refundable after generation work has started or a paid credit has been used'. That leaves a narrow window in principle (a pack bought and not yet used) but no published process, deadline or address for asking, so treat a purchase as final.
Are the songs on the site real customer examples?

No, and the site says so. The examples page and llms.txt label every demo 'illustrative' and state they 'are not customer testimonials', and the About page notes its editorial byline is organizational rather than a named expert. That is unusually candid for this category - but it also means there is no independent sample of what a paid song sounds like.
Which AI models does it use?

Songs: Suno v5.5, model identifier chirp-v5.5, accessed through the YourMusic API. Lyrics: OpenAI GPT-5.5, model identifier gpt-5.5. Both are named in the Terms and referenced in the privacy policy, which also discloses that generation inputs go to those third parties. The Terms reserve the right to change generation providers.
Who can see a gift page once I send it?

Anyone with the link. The site states in pricing, privacy and About that published gift pages are public and are 'not recipient-only or password-protected', and a page may show the recipient name, sender name, message, cover image, audio and a lyrics snapshot. Keep that in mind before writing in private detail.
trial_checklist: Start with the free lyric draft and edit it before paying - the draft costs nothing, and the wording is the part of a gift song that a refund cannot fix afterwards

Use the 30-second previews on both versions to pick the arrangement rather than the song, then buy the $19.90 one-time pack unless you already know you are making three gifts this month - the monthly plan is only cheaper from the third song
Write the brief with concrete details (a place, a nickname, one specific evening) instead of adjectives; a gift song's weakness is generic lines, and the brief is the only lever you control for free
Check the lyric draft for anything that identifies the recipient too specifically before publishing the share page, because the page is public to anyone holding the link
Treat the included regenerate as your one real second chance on a paid pack and spend it on a different vocal or style direction rather than the same brief again
Assume no refund after generation starts and no appeal channel beyond support@meloletter.com - a $19.90 pack is small enough that the practical test is one song, not a batch
Re-check the pricing page before a repeat purchase: the Terms reserve the right to change prices, plans and generation providers at any time, and the model named today is Suno v5.5
rating_rationale: Job fit 4.3/5. The product does one job and does it with the right shape: a written brief becomes an editable lyric draft, then two sung versions, then a gift page, and the free preview sits before the paywall rather than after it. The deliverable is stated precisely (two versions, one regenerate, MP3s, share page), a one-time $19.90 pack exists beside the $9.90/month plan so a single gift does not require a subscription, and the model stack is named down to the identifier. It loses points for a free tier that is rationed by unpublished daily capacity, a regenerate allowance of one, and no example of a finished paid song - the demos are labelled illustrative. Transparency 3.5/5. The privacy policy is among the more specific in this catalog (named analytics with retention periods, GPC/DNT honored, Mixpanel region stated, masking described) and the acceptable-use policy has a working reporting and appeals process, but the commercial basics are missing: no operator, no jurisdiction or governing law, no postal address, and no refund policy page at all - only a single clause - plus a consent-free measurement stack on a site sold to gift buyers in Europe and a four-month-old domain that is one of eight products on one operator's nameserver pair. Strong documentation of data handling, incomplete documentation of who is selling and what happens to your money.

name: ReelBoop
best_for: Creators who want a trending short video - a K-pop dance, a duet, an outfit change, a pet bit or a product film - assembled from one or two of their own photos, and who would rather buy metered credits than take on another full editing suite or a model API account
price: Two ways to buy, both in USD and both metered per generation. Subscriptions: Creator $9.90/month for 200 credits, or $99/year for 2,400 credits shown as $8.25/month; Pro $29.90/month or $299/year for 9,600; Studio $59.90/month or $599/year for 24,000. Yearly allowances are released upfront and plan credits expire at the end of the billing period. One-time credit packs: $15 for 200 credits, $45 for 800 and $90 for 2,000, valid 365 days with no auto-renewal. Credit costs are printed per tool before you start: GPT Image 2.6 and Nano Banana 2.1 at 5 credits an image, Kling 3.0 Pro at 60 credits per 5-second clip, Seedance 2.5 at 100 credits per 5-second clip, and the product-film preset at 10 credits a generation. There is no free trial - the pricing FAQ says video generation requires credits. The annual discount is a flat ~17% on all three tiers ($99 against 12 x $9.90 = $118.80, $299 against $358.80, $599 against $718.80), the /zh/pricing mirror prints the same figures to the cent, and the refund policy restates the Creator monthly figure at $9.90 for 200 credits. Stripe handles payment; no purchase was attempted.
summary: ReelBoop is a trending-video studio: you pick a template from a catalogue of about sixty dance, duet, transformation, pet and product scenes, upload the one or two photos the template asks for, and get a vertical MP4 back. The catalogue is specific rather than generic - every card prints how many photos and how many seconds it needs, so 'LISA Tarantino AI Dance' reads '1 photo, 15s' and 'JISOO ADDICTED' reads '2 photos, 15s' before you commit. Underneath, different templates run different models, and the pricing page quotes each cost up front: Kling 3.0 Pro at 60 credits per 5-second clip, Seedance 2.5 at 100, Wan 2.2 I2V Fast for the product-film preset, and GPT Image 2.6 or Nano Banana 2.1 for stills. Generated clips land in private Cloudflare R2 storage with playback and download tied to the owning account, there is no public gallery, and a confirmed failed generation returns its reserved credits. Pricing is three metered subscription tiers or three one-time credit packs, with a 365-day expiry on pack credits and a 7-day refund window on an untouched pack. The parts that make it worth listing are the consent gate that actually blocks analytics until you accept, the per-model credit table, and the refund page - the parts a buyer should weigh are the missing operator identity and the absence of any free trial.
use_cases: Making a trend-shaped clip for Reels, Shorts or TikTok from photos you already have instead of filming or prompting a model
Two-person duets where each participant's face comes from a separate photo and the template handles the interaction
Product films from a single product photo for a store listing or a paid social variant
Testing whether per-generation credits on Kling 3.0 Pro or Seedance 2.5 beat a monthly subscription for occasional output
Making a pet or family-moment clip for a group chat without opening an editing timeline
pros: Analytics consent is enforced, not just described: the sign-in page serves an Accept All / Reject All banner, the privacy policy states that Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and PVUV load only 'when you accept non-essential cookies', and it names the specific data PVUV is kept away from - prompts, uploaded photos, email addresses, orders and private creation links

A real refund policy exists at /refund-policy (updated 2026-11-13): a full refund within 7 days of buying a pack if none of its credits have been used, 365-day pack validity, credits returned for a confirmed failed generation, and a reviewed credit refund if you are unhappy with a delivered clip

Per-model credit costs are printed rather than hidden behind a plan: 5 credits per image on GPT Image 2.6 and Nano Banana 2.1, 60 credits per 5-second Kling 3.0 Pro clip, 100 for Seedance 2.5, 10 per product-film generation, with the model named in each tool

Prices agree across surfaces: the English pricing page, the /zh/pricing mirror and the refund policy all print $9.90 / $29.90 / $59.90 monthly, $99 / $299 / $599 yearly and $15 / $45 / $90 for the 200 / 800 / 2,000-credit packs, and the stated ~17% annual saving reconciles to the cent on every tier

Output is private by default: reference images and finished films sit in private Cloudflare R2 storage, playback and download require the owning account, and the site states there is no public gallery

Failures are handled in policy and in copy: rejected inputs are stopped before generation, and the pricing page promises credits back for confirmed failures with ambiguous requests checked before they are resolved

The legal set is written for this product and dated after the domain existed - Privacy 2026-10-13 and Terms plus Refund Policy 2026-11-13 against an RDAP registration of 2026-10-12 - and it names its processors: Cloudflare R2 for storage, Replicate for generation, SeeAPI for media checks, and a ten-minute expiring link when a review provider has to see a file
The catalogue is large and concrete - roughly sixty templates, each printing its photo count and duration, from Kling and Seedance video scenes to still-image tools
cons: No registered company, trading name, postal address or named data controller appears anywhere on the site, and the Terms carry no governing-law, jurisdiction, venue or arbitration clause - 'company', 'entity', 'jurisdiction', 'governing', 'laws of' and 'controller' all occur zero times across /privacy-policy and /terms-of-service
There is no free trial and no free allowance: the FAQ says plainly that video generation requires credits, so the cheapest way in is a $9.90 month or a $15 pack

Plan credits expire at the end of the billing period even on the annual plans, where the whole year's allowance is released upfront - a buyer who slows down loses the balance rather than rolling it over

/api/config/public returns email_verification_enabled:false and password_reset_enabled:false, so a mistyped signup address cannot be confirmed and a forgotten password has no in-product recovery path; support has to fix either by hand

Template cost is invisible until you sign in: the catalogue cards print photo count and duration, but the credit price for a given template appears only in the generator after login, and the spread between models is large - 5 credits for an image against 100 for a Seedance clip
Output rights are not granted anywhere: the Terms say to review results 'before sharing or commercial use' but never state what licence the buyer gets in the finished clip
No retention period is published for private creations - the policy says they are stored in R2 and that a ten-minute review link expires, but not how long an account's own history is kept

The model line-up moves quickly and the credit cost varies by up to 20x between models, so a price quoted from today's page may not describe the same clip next month; check the tool page immediately before buying
Thirty-eight days old at check, with no independent review or user report found
key_features: A catalogue of roughly sixty photo-to-video templates for dance trends, duets, outfit and character transformations, pets and product films, each labelled with the photos and seconds it needs
One or two photos in, vertical MP4 out, with the finished file kept privately in account history
Per-tool model choice where the template allows it - GPT Image 2.6 and Nano Banana 2.1 for stills, Kling 3.0 Pro and Seedance 2.5 for video, Wan 2.2 I2V Fast behind the product-film preset
Credit cost quoted per generation before you start, with a stated policy that confirmed failures return reserved credits
Three metered subscription tiers ($9.90 / $29.90 / $59.90 a month, ~17% off annually) and three one-time packs ($15 / $45 / $90) that do not auto-renew
Email-and-password accounts with an Accept All / Reject All cookie banner and analytics held until consent
Blog and model guides written for the same workflows - clip selection, product demos, multi-reference video - rather than thin SEO filler
faq: What does ReelBoop cost?

Two shapes, both metered in credits. Subscriptions are Creator at $9.90/month for 200 credits ($99/year for 2,400, shown as $8.25/month), Pro at $29.90/month or $299/year for 9,600, and Studio at $59.90/month or $599/year for 24,000; the yearly discount is a flat ~17% and plan credits expire at the end of the period. One-time packs are $15 for 200 credits, $45 for 800 and $90 for 2,000, valid 365 days with no auto-renewal. What a clip costs depends on the model the template runs: 60 credits per 5-second Kling 3.0 Pro clip, 100 for Seedance 2.5, 10 for the product-film preset, and 5 for an image. There is no free trial.
Is there a free plan?

No. The pricing FAQ states that video generation requires credits, and no page offers a trial grant. The credit chip in the header reads 0 / 600 before sign-in, but that is a display default rather than a published allowance, and no page explains it - so budget either a $9.90 month or a $15 pack to try the product.
What happens if a generation fails?

Reserved credits are returned when a generation is confirmed failed. If a request is still processing or its outcome is unknown, the site says it checks the original request before resolving it, and asks you not to submit duplicates. The refund policy adds that a delivered clip you are unhappy with can be raised with support for a reviewed credit refund.
Can I use the videos commercially?

The Terms require you to have permission for the photos you upload and say to review outputs 'before sharing or commercial use', which implies commercial use is contemplated, but no page grants a licence in the finished clip or states who owns it. Ask before using an output in paid advertising.
Do I need an account, and how do I get back in if I lose the password?

Yes - email and password accounts, and generation is gated behind sign-in. The public config reports password reset and email verification as disabled, so a forgotten password or a typo in the signup address has to be sorted out with support@reelboop.com rather than through the product.
trial_checklist: Decide the model before the template: the same 5-second clip costs 60 credits on Kling 3.0 Pro and 100 on Seedance 2.5, so the pack you buy depends on which one your template runs
Start with the $15 pack rather than a month if you only want one or two clips - pack credits last 365 days and do not auto-renew, while monthly credits vanish at period end
Check the credit price on the template page after signing in, because the public catalogue prints photos and seconds but not cost
Download the MP4 the same day and keep your own copy - output lives in private R2 storage and no retention period for account history is published
Ask support@reelboop.com in writing what licence you get in the finished clip if you plan to use it for a client or an ad, since the Terms do not say
rating_rationale: Job fit 4.0/5. The catalogue is specific and checkable rather than a prompt box: roughly sixty templates, each printing the photos and seconds it needs, with per-model credit costs on the pricing page and again on each tool. The models named are real and current - Kling 3.0 Pro shipped from Kuaishou in February 2026, Seedance 2.5 and Nano Banana 2.1 are in release, and GPT Image 2.6 is the image model other sites in this catalogue already run - so nothing here depends on a model that does not exist. The commercial machinery holds up under arithmetic: the ~17% annual discount reconciles on all three tiers, the packs are priced per credit consistently ($15/200, $45/800, $90/2,000), the refund policy restates the same Creator figure, and the Chinese mirror prints identical numbers. Failures are covered in policy and privacy is real - R2 private storage, no public gallery, an expiring review link, and analytics that wait for an Accept All / Reject All choice. What holds job fit below 4.2 is the absence of any free trial at a $15 minimum and the missing output-licence sentence. Transparency 3.8/5. In its favour: a product-specific refund page, three named processors, a consent gate enforced in the UI, and legal pages dated after the registration. Against: no operator, controller, address or governing law; no retention schedule for account history; and email verification and password reset both switched off in the public config, which leaves account recovery to a support thread. The score is the average of the two, split here so the number can be audited against the pages rather than read as a single impression.

name: StylMorph
best_for: People who want one photo redrawn as comic art, a cartoon or a game-art frame without opening Photoshop - and who also want a free browser toolbox for crops, borders, watermarks and format conversions that never uploads the file
price: Free to try once: one successful Seedream 4.5 image per guest identity, no account, shared across the site's image tools. Then one-time credit packs with no subscription and no auto-renewal - Starter $6.99 for 40 credits ($0.175 per credit), Creator $12.99 for 90 ($0.144) and Studio $24.99 for 200 ($0.125) - and purchased credits never expire. Cost per image depends on the model: Seedream 4.5 is 1 credit, Nano Banana Pro is 4 purchased credits, and the fixed two-model comparison is 2 purchased credits, so a Seedream image is about $0.06 on the largest pack and a Nano Banana Pro image about $0.50. Nano Banana Pro and comparisons cannot be paid for with free or gifted credits. Checkout is by Stripe after Google sign-in, the cost is quoted before each generation, and results are downloadable for 24 hours. No purchase was attempted.
summary: StylMorph is a browser image transformer with a wider toolbox around it. The paid centre of it is an image-to-image tool: upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 10 MB, pick an inked, halftone, cel-shaded, storybook or game-art treatment, compare the result against the original with a slider and download. Two models sit behind it - Seedream 4.5 at 1 credit an image and Nano Banana Pro at 4 purchased credits - plus a fixed two-model comparison for 2 credits, and a single free Seedream render per guest identity to test with. Around that it ships roughly thirty free browser-local utilities that the pricing page says do not upload your image at all: crop and straighten, add text, watermarks and borders, circle crops, rainbow profile frames, Instagram grids, colour-picker and palette tools, Base64 and metadata viewers, and JPG/PNG/WebP/AVIF converters. Pricing is three one-time packs whose per-credit prices reconcile exactly with the printed figures, credits that never expire, and results that expire after 24 hours on every plan. The privacy notice is the most specific in this batch - named analytics, a masked Clarity canvas, hashed addresses for quota, signed short-lived links - and the gap is where most of these sites leave it: no operator, no governing law, and no refund page beyond a 14-day clause for duplicate or undelivered charges.
use_cases: Turning one portrait or pet photo into comic, cartoon or game-art art for a profile picture or a print
Comparing Seedream 4.5 against Nano Banana Pro on the same photo and style before committing credits
Batch-restyling a small set of images for a shop listing, a poster or a thumbnail sheet
Doing quick crops, borders, watermarks and format conversions in the browser without uploading the file anywhere
Testing whether per-image credits beat a monthly image-generator subscription for occasional work
pros: The privacy notice is unusually concrete for a small tool: it names Google Analytics 4, Microsoft Clarity and PVUV as the only optional analytics, states that they load only with permission, says the private image canvas is explicitly masked so uploads never reach Clarity, and describes signed short-lived links, a signed browser identifier, a one-way network-address representation for quota, Cloudflare Turnstile and Stripe by name
An explicit 'Analytics choices' control sits in the footer, so a visitor can withdraw consent after the fact rather than being asked once and never again

The pack arithmetic reconciles exactly: 40 credits at $0.175 is $7.00 and the card charges $6.99, 90 at $0.144 is $12.96 and the card charges $12.99, 200 at $0.125 is $25.00 and the card charges $24.99, and each card prints its own per-credit figure and its discount against Starter

Purchased credits never expire and nothing auto-renews - the pack page says both, and the FAQ repeats them - which is rare in this category where most competitors sell monthly image credits that reset

One genuinely free render per guest identity lets a buyer judge output quality on their own photo before paying, and the site is explicit that the allowance is shared across its image tools rather than one per tool
Roughly thirty free utilities that the pricing page says run in the browser and do not upload images, which is a real second product rather than a landing page
Both policies are dated 2026-09-20, after the domain's RDAP registration of 2026-08-31, and are written for an image product rather than pasted from another one
Failure handling is stated: a confirmed failure returns the reserved credits once or releases the reserved free allowance, and an uncertain request keeps its reservation while the original is checked
cons: Originals and results expire after 24 hours on every plan, including the paid packs - the pricing page says 'Private result access for 24 hours' on the Starter card and the privacy notice confirms originals and results are designed to expire automatically - so this is a make-and-download tool, not an archive
Google is the only way to sign in, and signing in is required to buy and to carry a credit balance across devices

No refund policy page exists: /refund-policy and /legal both 404, and the only refund language is a 14-day clause in the pricing FAQ and Terms covering duplicate charges, unauthorized payments and credits that were not delivered, with delivered credit purchases 'generally final'
No registered company, trading name, postal address or named data controller appears anywhere, and neither policy carries a governing-law, jurisdiction or venue clause

Task records may outlive the images: the policy says technical records can be retained after the 24-hour image links expire, without stating a period
Nano Banana Pro and the two-model comparison require purchased credits, so the free render only tests the cheaper model

The ShipAny starter's own pricing payload is still in the page source - the shipped config carries 'Starter $99 / Standard $199 / Premium $299', 'Get ShipAny' calls to action, Supabase and Vercel copy - with zero occurrences in rendered text, so it is build residue rather than an offer, but it is a route that could surface if the template is ever rendered

faq: What does StylMorph cost?

One free Seedream 4.5 image per guest identity, then one-time credit packs with no subscription: $6.99 for 40 credits ($0.175 each), $12.99 for 90 ($0.144) and $24.99 for 200 ($0.125). Is there a free trial?

There is one free successful Seedream 4.5 image per guest browser identity, available without an account and shared across the site's image tools. How long are my images kept?

Originals and results are designed to expire after 24 hours on every plan, paid packs included, and the download button is the only way to keep one. Technical task records may be retained beyond that, but the policy does not state for how long.
Can I get a refund?

Do the free tools upload my photos?

trial_checklist: Use the free Seedream render on the photo you actually care about first - it is the only way to judge the style presets on your own material, and it does not test Nano Banana Pro
Download the result immediately: originals and outputs expire after 24 hours even on a paid pack, and there is no archive to come back to

Ask support@stylmorph.com about commercial use before publishing an output for a client - neither policy states what licence the buyer gets in the generated image
rating_rationale: Job fit 3.9/5. The core job - one photo in, a styled image out, with a before/after compare and a download - is described and priced precisely enough to judge before buying: nine named presets, two named models, per-model credit costs, and a pack ladder whose arithmetic reconciles on every card. The free render is a real trial rather than a marketing claim, and the surrounding browser tools are a second product that costs nothing. What holds it under 4.2 is the 24-hour expiry on paid output, Google-only sign-in, and a one-credit-versus-four-credit model split that quietly turns the cheapest pack into ten Nano Banana images rather than forty. The gaps are the ones this catalogue keeps finding - no operator, controller, address or governing law, no refund page, an unnamed AI provider, and task records outliving the images without a stated period. The score averages the two and is split so a reader can see which half pulled it down.

name: FicWeave
best_for: Fanfiction and original-fiction writers who want a saved, chapter-by-chapter manuscript with a visible, source-linked memory of characters, relationships and open plot threads - instead of re-pasting a growing context into a chat window every chapter
price: Subscriptions only, in USD, plus a one-time free allowance rather than a trial. Free after sign-in: 3 starter credits that do not expire, 1 editable story, read-only Story Memory and up to one recent chapter of context. Pro $7.99/month for 100 credits per subscription month and up to 20 editable stories; Pro+ $14.99/month for 200 credits and 50 stories; Max $24.99/month for 400 credits and 100 stories. Annual billing charges once and grants credits monthly: $79.90, $149.90 and $249.90, which is exactly ten monthly payments and matches the 'Save 16.7%' badge on every card; the /zh/pricing mirror prints the same figures to the cent and the Terms restate both columns. A saved standard continuation costs 1 credit; a failed or cancelled attempt returns its reservation to its original source and expiry; Story Memory updates cost nothing. Subscription credits expire at each monthly window with no rollover, on annual plans too. One-time Credit Packs are no longer sold - /pricing, /terms, /refund-policy and /contact each say so - and only prior purchases keep their historical terms. All six SKUs (three plans x monthly/annual) report ready:true at /api/payment/checkout-readiness; the Choose buttons ship disabled in the served HTML and enable after the client-side account check. Waffo Pancake is the merchant of record for checkout, tax and the customer portal. No purchase was attempted.
summary: FicWeave is a single-purpose writing workspace for fanfiction. You give it a fandom or an original universe, the characters, a relationship or trope and a one-line what-if, and it writes a first chapter you can read without an account; saving the story creates a private library and a continuation workspace. Each continuation is assembled from selected Story Memory - Characters, Relationships, Important Facts, Open Threads and a bounded summary, with every AI-created item labelled by the chapter it came from - plus recent chapters (one on Free, up to six on paid plans). The claim being sold is workflow, not prose: the FAQ says outright that FicWeave 'does not promise better prose than ChatGPT or perfect continuity', and its own case-study page discloses an earlier failed extraction and a remaining continuity error rather than presenting a clean benchmark. All three paid plans run 'the same Pro writing model capability', so the ladder buys credits and editable-story slots rather than a better model. It is 18+, the Content Policy bans explicit sexual content and any sexualisation of minors or identifiable real people, and the Terms state that FicWeave is not affiliated with or endorsed by any fandom, franchise or author a user writes with.
use_cases: Drafting a multi-chapter fanfic where chapter twelve still has to remember a detail from chapter two
Exploring what-if branches inside a fandom you already write in, without re-pasting canon and context every chapter
Original long-form fiction that needs a tracked cast, established facts and unresolved threads instead of one long prompt
Testing whether a paid AI writing subscription earns its price by spending the one-time free allowance first
Correcting a story's continuity directly - paid plans let you edit a remembered character fact before the next chapter
pros: Every processor is named with its purpose rather than described by category: Cloudflare for delivery, hosting and security, Neon for the hosted PostgreSQL database, OpenRouter and the model providers it routes to for generation, Waffo Pancake for checkout, tax, fraud checks and prompt screening, Google for sign-in and Analytics, and Resend for transactional email

The privacy policy states plainly that private story text is not used to train a FicWeave model and that personal information is not sold, and it separates its own practice from what third-party model providers may do instead of calling the whole chain private

Credit mechanics are unusually honest: 1 credit per saved continuation, nothing charged for a failed or cancelled attempt (the reservation returns to its original source and expiry), nothing charged for Story Memory updates, and saved stories and chapters stay readable when credits run out

It publishes its own limits instead of overselling them - /llms.txt says the Story Memory case study is 'not a published generation-quality benchmark', records an earlier truncation and a failed extraction, and admits a continuity error that remained; the generator FAQ says the sample chapter is an authored illustration, not an AI generation

The free allowance is described exactly rather than advertised as a free plan: first chapter with no account, then 3 non-expiring starter credits, 1 editable story, read-only memory, and the context difference stated as 'Free uses up to 1 recent chapter; paid plans use up to 6'

The Content Policy is explicit in both directions - what is allowed (romance, dark themes, fictional violence, non-explicit mature themes) and what is refused (explicit sexual content, sexualisation of minors, non-consensual explicit content, sexualisation of real people, moderation evasion) - with an 18+ requirement in the Terms

Email verification and password reset are both enabled in /api/config/public, so a mistyped address or a forgotten password has a recovery path - several listings in this catalogue ship with one or both switched off
Pricing reconciles across every surface that states it: /pricing, /zh/pricing, /terms and /refund-policy agree on all six figures, and the annual column is exactly ten monthly payments
cons: No registered company, trading name, postal address or named data controller appears on any page: the Terms define the counterparty only as 'the independent operator of the Service' and the privacy policy as 'the independent operator of FicWeave', and there is no governing-law, jurisdiction, venue or arbitration clause - the Terms end at 'Changes and contact'

Google Analytics 4 (G-YPKFQG4WCL) loads on first paint on every page, including /privacy itself, with no consent banner anywhere on the site, while the policy says processing rests on consent 'where consent is required' - a reader in the EU or UK is measured before making any choice
The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon (static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js) also ships sitewide, and the policy names Cloudflare for delivery, hosting and security but never for analytics
Self-service export and permanent account deletion are described in the policy as things that are 'not yet complete features', so the only route to your own data is an email to support

Subscription credits expire at the end of each monthly window with no rollover, including on annual plans where the full year is paid up front - three quiet months on an annual plan still burns three allowances

All three paid plans run the same writing model, so $24.99/month buys 400 credits and 100 editable stories rather than better output; the site says this, but a capacity ladder priced like a quality ladder is easy to misread

Fanfiction output depends on rights the writer holds: the Terms put responsibility for third-party characters and settings on the user and disclaim any affiliation with or endorsement by the fandoms and authors involved

Retention is phrased rather than periodised - story data lasts 'while your account and saved content remain active', diagnostics and logs 'only as reasonably needed', backups 'a limited period' - and no number is given for any of them
key_features: An anonymous first chapter: fandom, characters, relationship, trope and a what-if in, a readable chapter out, no account needed
A private story library with chapter navigation and a continuation workspace rather than one growing chat thread
Story Memory over five fields - Characters, Relationships, Important Facts, Open Threads and a bounded summary - with every AI-created item labelled by its source chapter
Editable memory on paid plans, with user edits protected from later AI updates, plus Mark resolved / Mark dropped on open threads
Bounded context assembly: selected memory, a summary and recent chapters (one on Free, six on paid), explicitly not the whole manuscript
English and Chinese mirrors of every public page under /zh, prices identical to the cent
Email/password and Google sign-in, with email verification and password reset enabled
faq: What does FicWeave cost?

Subscriptions only, in USD: Pro $7.99/month for 100 credits per subscription month and up to 20 editable stories, Pro+ $14.99/month for 200 credits and 50 stories, Max $24.99/month for 400 credits and 100 stories. Annual billing is $79.90, $149.90 and $249.90, charged once with credits granted monthly - exactly ten monthly payments, the 'Save 16.7%' the cards advertise. A saved standard continuation costs 1 credit. One-time credit packs are no longer sold, and subscription credits expire at each monthly window without rollover.
Is there a free trial?

No trial and no card-free paid tier. What exists is a one-time free allowance: the first chapter can be generated and read with no account at all, and after sign-in Free includes 3 starter credits that do not expire, 1 editable story, read-only Story Memory and up to one recent chapter of context. A card is only involved when you buy a paid plan.
Can I keep my stories and chapters if I stop paying?

Yes. Saved stories, chapters and Story Memory stay readable, and stories outside your plan's editable set become read-only rather than deleted - the pricing page and Terms both say the content is not removed. New chapters and edits need credits and an editable slot.
Does FicWeave train on my stories?

The privacy policy says private story text is not used to train a FicWeave model and that personal information is not sold. Story input and context are sent to OpenRouter, which routes to the selected model provider, and the policy states that those providers' retention and data-use rules differ by model and endpoint - so the vendor's promise covers its own model, not the whole chain.
Does it write explicit content?

No. The Content Policy allows romance, dark themes, fictional violence and non-explicit mature themes, and refuses explicit sexual content, any sexualisation of minors, non-consensual explicit content, sexualisation of identifiable real people and instructions for evading moderation. The Terms require users to be 18 or older.
How is this different from writing fanfiction in a chat window?

A saved library, chapter navigation, a continuation workspace and a source-linked memory panel you can read and correct - versus re-supplying context in every prompt. The vendor frames this as a workflow difference and explicitly does not claim better prose than ChatGPT or perfect continuity; continuation uses selected memory, a summary and recent chapters rather than the whole manuscript.
trial_checklist: Generate the anonymous first chapter before creating any account - it costs nothing and no card is involved, and it is the only honest test of whether the prose voice suits you
Spend the 3 starter credits on continuations rather than buying a plan, then check whether chapter 2 actually uses the memory items extracted from chapter 1
Check the Memory panel against the chapter it cites: each AI-created item names its source chapter, so a wrong relationship or fact is visible before you pay for the right to edit it
Size the plan by your own pace - 1 credit per saved chapter means Pro's 100 credits is 100 saved continuations a month, and whatever you do not use expires at the window end
If you write slowly, take monthly over annual even at the 16.7% discount: an annual plan pays for twelve allowances up front and a quiet quarter still expires three of them

Before any annual payment, email support@ficweave.com for the operator's legal name and governing law - neither is published anywhere on the site, and the refund policy is non-refundable once a period begins
rating_rationale: Job fit 4.2/5. This is a narrow, real product rather than a prompt box with a fandom dropdown: the memory is source-linked and reviewable, free and paid differ in stated ways (one recent chapter against six, read-only against editable memory), the credit rules are written where a buyer can act on them, and the free path needs no account or card. The three paid tiers differ only in credits and editable-story slots, which the site states rather than implying a model upgrade. Transparency 3.9/5, bringing the score to 4.0. In its favour: every processor named with a purpose, an explicit no-training statement for the vendor's own model, a content policy with real limits, a refund policy, and marketing copy that discloses its own sample chapter as authored and its own case study as not a benchmark. Against it: no operator, postal address or governing law anywhere on the site; GA4 and the Cloudflare analytics beacon load on the policy page itself with no consent gate while the policy relies on consent; self-service export and account deletion are not built; monthly credit expiry applies even to annual plans; and retention is phrased rather than periodised. None of those is a reader-protection gate - the product is purchasable, priced, describable and uncontested in name - so they are published as cons rather than held, which is what keeps the score at 4.0 instead of higher.

price: Monthly subscriptions in EUR plus VAT, sold through a request form rather than a checkout, with a free tier. Annual billing is a 20% discount over twelve monthly payments, paid once for the year, with the credits still granted monthly rather than all at once; no annual figure is published anywhere on the page, so the discounted total has to be computed from the monthly price. Unused credits roll over into one additional monthly period and expire at the end of it, oldest credits consumed first; cancelling a monthly plan runs to the end of the paid month, and cancelling an annual plan stops renewal while access and the monthly credit grants continue to the end of the paid year. Enterprise is custom - agreed capacity, tailored integrations, a forward deployed engineer, DPA and security review, adapted invoicing. The pricing FAQ states 'there is no online checkout yet' and that the team confirms access, configuration and billing before anything is charged. No purchase was attempted.
summary: Markin is an agentic growth platform for large direct-to-consumer businesses. You connect a store, CRM and warehouse; its agents read customer behaviour, propose revenue opportunities with a size attached, prepare or launch the intervention in the tools you already run, and read each result against a control group. The pitch is deliberately narrow - incremental ARPU, not more dashboards - and the vendor is unusually candid on its own comparison page that an LLM wired to your data through MCP can do parts of this work; what it sells is the assembled system, the experiment bookkeeping, the audit trail and the team that stands behind it. Access is sales-led: the free allowance and every paid plan begin with a request form, and the pricing FAQ says outright that there is no online checkout yet.

Running more experiments in parallel than a small data-science team can staff, each with a holdout
Turning a CRM audit into a sized list of opportunities with owners
Letting lifecycle teams ship 1:1 next-best-action decisions through tools they already pay for

cons: There is no self-serve path at all: the free card's button reads 'Request free access', the Pro card's reads 'Request Pro', and 'Get started for free' in the navigation lands on the same /apply form - no signup, no card entry, no workspace to look at before a sales call, so a reader cannot evaluate the product today the way they can a $9 tool

name: TINY DESK AI (tiny-deskai.net)
best_for: People who want to put themselves and a couple of friends into the 'Outstanding' Tiny Desk meme - a 15-second desk-concert clip for a TikTok, Reel or Short - from photos they already have, and would rather buy a small one-time video pack than start another monthly AI video subscription. Not for anyone needing high resolution, batch output, or a clear answer on what music the finished video carries.
price: One-time video packs only, no subscription and no auto-renewal, priced in USD: 1 video $5.90 ($5.90 per video), 3 videos $15.90 ($5.30 per video) and 10 videos $49.90 ($4.99 per video). Each pack is 1, 3 or 10 video credits and each generated video uses 1 credit. Output is a 15-second 480p clip with audio included, in vertical 9:16 or widescreen 16:9, from one required lead portrait plus up to two optional bandmate photos. Checkout is through Waffo Pancake; the public status endpoint returns paymentMode 'live' and paymentProvider 'waffo', and the pricing buttons render 'Sign in to buy' for a signed-in Google account. A confirmed failed generation returns the credit automatically. The studio caps generation at 2 attempts per account per 24 hours, subject to capacity, with one video in progress at a time. The per-video arithmetic reconciles on every row (5.90/1 = 5.90, 15.90/3 = 5.30, 49.90/10 = 4.99) and the same figures appear on the homepage, /pricing and the pricing FAQ. No purchase was attempted.
summary: TINY DESK AI (tiny-deskai.net) is a single-purpose browser studio for the 'Outstanding' Tiny Desk meme: it turns one lead portrait plus up to two optional bandmate photos into a 15-second 480p desk-concert video, with audio included, in a vertical or widescreen frame. You pick a room concept (The Soul Session, The Outstanding Moment, The Indie Room), cast a lead singer and optional keyboard and sax players, tick a photo-permission checkbox and a separate processing consent, sign in with Google and spend 1 video credit. Draft preparation is free and local - selecting photos and saving a draft uploads nothing; photos reach kie.ai's file service and Seedance only after you explicitly confirm generation. It sells one-time video packs ($5.90 for 1, $15.90 for 3, $49.90 for 10) through Waffo Pancake, returns the credit on a confirmed failed generation, and caps output at 2 attempts per account per 24 hours. The site is six days old and unusually plain-spoken about its own limits: it disclaims any NPR affiliation, labels its scene concepts 'NOT A GENERATED RESULT', discloses that provider media URLs are accessible to anyone with the link, and names its processors and their retention windows. What it does not yet resolve is who operates it, what audio the finished video actually carries, and why its privacy notice still says generation is disabled while the live status endpoint enables it.
use_cases: Casting yourself as the lead singer and two friends as the band in a 15-second desk-concert meme clip
A vertical 9:16 or widescreen 16:9 novelty video for a group chat, birthday post or social reply, made from portraits instead of filming
Testing whether a pay-per-video pack ($5.90 for one) beats a monthly AI video subscription for a one-off trend clip
Comparing a photo-to-video meme studio against prompt-driven generators that guess the scene from text
Preparing a cast and saving draft settings for free before deciding whether to buy a credit
pros: It is live and purchasable, and the machine-readable state agrees with the rendered page: GET /api/status returns videoGeneration:true, payments:true, paymentMode:'live', paymentProvider:'waffo' and generation.enabled:true (duration 15, resolution 480p, creditsPerVideo 1, dailyLimit 2); the three pricing buttons render 'Sign in to buy' (active, not disabled); /api/generate answers 405 to a GET (a real POST route) and /api/billing/credits answers 401 'Sign in to view credits.' This is not a pre-launch page despite the 'first session' framing

The pricing reconciles on every row and across three surfaces: $5.90/1, $15.90/3 and $49.90/10 print the same per-video figures ($5.90, $5.30, $4.99) on the homepage, /pricing and the pricing FAQ, one-time with no subscription, and a confirmed failed generation returns the credit automatically

An explicit NPR non-affiliation disclaimer in the footer and the FAQ: 'An independent AI project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by NPR, Tiny Desk Concerts, Charlie Wilson or The Gap Band', and the FAQ answers 'Is this affiliated with NPR or Tiny Desk Concerts? No.' For a product built on NPR's trademarked format, saying so plainly is worth crediting

Draft preparation is genuinely local and the upload is gated behind consent: the privacy notice states 'Selecting photos and saving a draft do not upload image files. Refreshing or leaving the studio clears photo selections', and the studio requires a photo-permission checkbox plus a separate 'I agree to send these photos to kie.ai and its video-processing providers' confirmation before anything is sent

Processors and provider retention are named rather than gestured at: kie.ai's file service (kieai.redpandaai.co) and Seedance for generation, Cloudflare R2 for completed-video copies, Google for sign-in and Waffo for checkout, with the provider windows stated (uploads deleted after 24 hours, generated files retained 14 days) and the honest caveat that 'these are provider policies, not deletion controls operated by this site'

It discloses its own risks instead of hiding them: 'Provider uploads and generated results use accessible media URLs. A substantive Acceptable Use & Content Policy: adults 18+, named prohibited-content categories, manual review with a 2-business-day acknowledgement target and a 7-day decision target, an appeal route, and 'no blanket no-refund rule for reported accounts' - refunds are reviewed individually rather than forfeited on an allegation

Honest example labelling and a working domain contact: scene concepts are marked 'SCENE CONCEPT - NOT A GENERATED RESULT', the /outstanding artwork is called 'AI concept artwork... not original concert footage', and support@tiny-deskai.net is a real mailbox (RCPT 250 against a 550 random-local-part control at the domain's Cloudflare MX, so not a catch-all), printed in the footer and both policies. The legal set is dated 16-17 November 2026, after the domain was registered on 13 November
cons: No registered company, trading name, postal address or named data controller appears anywhere, and the Terms carry no governing-law, jurisdiction, venue or arbitration clause - 'company', 'entity', 'jurisdiction', 'governing', 'laws of' and 'controller' occur zero times across /privacy, /terms and /acceptable-use (the 'Inc' substring hits are the word 'including'), re-checked 2026-11-19

The homepage 'illustrative preview' is the actual viral meme, not a buyer's result: the hero file /videos/hero-session-mobile-v1.mp4 (480x854, 17.5 s, H.264 + AAC) shows recognizable college-football coaches in Texas, Georgia, Indiana and Alabama gear - the original October 18 'Outstanding' TikTok - under the label 'Illustrative preview. The pricing cards say 'Audio included', but the site does not state what that audio is. The /outstanding page says the project 'does not supply the original song or recording', and the Terms grant 'no rights to third-party recordings, footage, songs, artist voices or trademarks'. Since the meme is defined by The Gap Band's 'Outstanding', ask the vendor whether the included audio is that recording, a soundalike or original music before buying for a public post.
What happens to my photos?

Selecting photos and saving a draft does not upload them; they stay in your browser until you tick the processing consent and generate. Then they are sent to kie.ai's file service (kieai.redpandaai.co) and Seedance, cropped and re-encoded without original metadata. The notice discloses that provider uploads and results use accessible media URLs - anyone with the link may reach them - that uploads are deleted after 24 hours and generated files kept 14 days by the provider, and that the site's own R2 copies have no automatic expiry or self-service deletion yet.
Is this affiliated with NPR?

No. The footer and FAQ state it is 'an independent AI project, not affiliated with or endorsed by NPR, Tiny Desk Concerts, Charlie Wilson or The Gap Band.' 'Tiny Desk' is NPR's trademark; the site is one of several independent tools riding the same meme, and its rights to the name are not confirmed.
What do I get back, and in what quality?

A 15-second 480p video with audio, in vertical 9:16 or widescreen 16:9, downloadable from your account history. There is no resolution above 480p and no length option. Likeness, singing and instrument motion vary, and the scene concepts are labelled 'NOT A GENERATED RESULT', so the preview is creative direction rather than a promise of the output.

A browser photo-enhancement service that rebuilds detail lost to blur, pixelation, grain or low resolution. You upload an image (JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC up to 20MB), pick 1K or 2K, and it returns a sharper version to compare against the original before you download. Neighbouring pages apply the same engine to specific jobs - blurry text, pixelated images, faces, old prints, colourising, print preparation and pulling a still from a video - and it will not attempt to strip censorship, mosaics or paywall blur.

faq: What is GTA6 AI Video?

An independent web app that creates GTA-inspired fan videos from your photos. You browse a prepared GTA 6 or GTA 5 scene, add a photo for each required role - or start from your own prompt, still or reference clip - review the model, duration and credit estimate, and generate. Finished clips appear in My creations for review and download. It is not an official game product and the site says so itself.
How much does GTA6 AI Video cost?

The free plan gives 20 one-time signup credits plus a weekly check-in worth 60 credits across a seven-day cycle, with watermarked downloads and roughly three images or one video before you pay. Subscriptions are Starter $22.90/mo for 840 credits, Creator $48.90/mo for 1,800 and Studio $98.90/mo for 3,650, or yearly at $218.90, $410.90 and $593.40 (each exactly twelve monthly payments). One-time packs that never expire run from $8.99 for 300 credits to $918.90 for 44,000. Usage is quoted at 6 credits per image and 18 per video on the cheapest models.
Do the credits expire?

It depends on how you bought them. Subscription credits expire at the end of their billing period and renew with an active plan; credits from a one-time pack never expire. Promotional credits follow whatever expiry is shown when they are granted, and the free plan's 20 signup credits are issued with a 365-day expiry in the site's own configuration.
Is this an official GTA 6 tool?

No. The site's own FAQ states that GTA6 AI Video is an independent service, not affiliated with or endorsed by Rockstar Games or the owners of Grand Theft Auto, and that it is not an official game, release, game editor or access to unreleased gameplay. GTA 6 itself launched on 2026-11-19; this domain was registered the same day.
Can I use the videos commercially?

The Terms say you own the outputs generated for your account, but commercial-use rights are not settled model by model - the pricing FAQ answers the question by telling buyers to review the Terms, applicable law and 'restrictions for the chosen model'. Treat commercial use as unresolved until the vendor says which models permit it.
Who operates the site, and where is the company?

The site names no company, trading name, postal address or jurisdiction anywhere - the Privacy controller block and the Terms contact clause both list only 'GTA6 AI Video' with a support@gta6ai.video address, and the governing-law clause refers to 'the jurisdiction where GTA6 AI Video is established' without naming it. That is an open item, not a settled fact.
What do I need to sign up?

A Google account. Google is the only sign-in the shipped configuration enables (credential and GitHub login are off), and purchase requires signing in so credits attach to that account. There is also no self-service account deletion - deletion is requested by email to support@gta6ai.video.

faq: What is MiniMax H3 Image?

A browser studio that generates images and video from prompts or reference files using a catalogue of current third-party models on one credit balance. It is named after MiniMax's H3-Image model, which its image tool offers first, but it is a multi-model workspace rather than a single-model generator: stills can also run on GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream, Qwen Image, FLUX, Ideogram, Recraft or Z-Image, and video on Seedance, Kling, Veo, Wan, Grok Imagine, Gemini Omni or MiniMax H3 and its Max variants. Nothing is installed locally.
How much does it cost?

Monthly billing is Lite $12.99 for 3,000 credits, Pro $34.99 for 10,000 and Ultra $129.99 for 30,000 a month. Billed yearly the same tiers are $9.99, $24.99 and $79.99 a month, charged as $119.88, $299.88 and $959.88 a year, with the credits released monthly. One-time packs that stay valid 365 days cost $29.99 for 5,000 credits up to $899.99 for 250,000. Every model draws on the same balance and the cost of a generation is shown before you submit it.
Does MiniMax H3 generate the images?

On this site the image tool offers MiniMax H3 Image as its first listed model, costing 11 credits for a 1:1 image at 2K in the tool's default state, alongside an H3 Image Highspeed variant. What happens if a generation fails?

Credits are deducted when a task is submitted and returned automatically if it fails, including failures caused by content safety review or copyright restrictions. The Terms and the pricing FAQ say the same thing, and the credit history in the account shows the status of each task.
Do credits expire?

Subscription credits expire at the next monthly refresh and do not roll over; one-time pack credits stay valid for 365 days. When credits with different expiry dates are on the account the soonest to expire are used first, and a later purchase does not extend earlier credits.
Who operates the site?

The Terms are governed by no named jurisdiction. That is worth knowing before you pay, because it is the operator a buyer would have to pursue rather than a registered entity.

faq: Who operates PoseLoop?

poseloop.app is operated by ZheLogic, LLC, a limited liability company established in the State of Delaware, United States, which the Privacy Policy also names as the operator and data controller. What does PoseLoop cost?

Within 7 days of buying a credit pack or the first charge of a subscription, if the credits are substantially unspent, write to support@poseloop.app; approved payments take 5-10 business days to return via the original route. The Free plan is $0 with 10 credits. Personal is $10.00/month, or $9.00/month billed annually at $108.00, for 500 credits a month ($0.018/credit).
